_comment: The Hardware-medal ladder + its PRICE — the ONE shared contract between the money path and the credential wall, which live in different packages. lambda/qpu/qpu-core.test.mjs asserts the real constants in qpu-core.mjs still match this file AND that the advertised cheapest path is really the cheapest (the price lock). web/__tests__/lib/credentials.test.ts asserts HARDWARE_TIERS in web/src/lib/credentials.ts still matches it. Neither suite hand-copies the other's numbers, so a change on EITHER side fails loudly here instead of silently shipping a ladder whose advertised price is wrong. The sponsored allowance was WITHDRAWN on 2026-07-28: the ladder is now bought with credits, and grandfatheredCapMicros is only the cap already stamped on pre-existing learners' ledger rows, kept so their tests and their allowance stay honest. Do not add a tier without re-running the lock.

cheapestPath._comment: The cheapest way to hold ALL THREE medals at once: 3 runs whose shots sum to 1,000. Cost depends only on (runs, shots) — never on how the shots are split across the runs — so any 334/333/333-style split costs the same. 300000*3 + 1450*1000 = 2350000 micros = $2.35 = 235 credits to hold the whole ladder.
